WITHDRAWN_consequence_do_not_quote.WITHDRAWN: superseded by the_size_question_answered_without_the_capacity_study and the corrected hurdle. Its 2.5% figure counts only the protocol fee; the real hurdle is 5.4% at 0.1 SOL. Its reasoning about size was right by accident. Kept so the error is visible, NOT to be quoted.
WITHDRAWN_consequence_do_not_quote.how_far_the_tested_signals_are_from_it: B19D tested five signals across 252 cells and none had a median above zero. B19F tested eight exit rules across 72 cells and none had a median above zero. The observed drift at immediate exit is 0.42 percent ADVERSE against a 2.5 percent hurdle.
WITHDRAWN_consequence_do_not_quote.the_hurdle_expressed_as_a_number: any strategy on this venue must produce more than approximately 2.5 percent of favourable price movement round trip, at any size, before it breaks even. That is the protocol's own fee schedule and no infrastructure improvement touches it.
WITHDRAWN_consequence_do_not_quote.the_obvious_next_move_and_why_it_fails: the fixed components are 2.25 percent of a 0.1 SOL position, so a larger position amortises them and the arithmetic looks rescuable. It is not. At 1 SOL the fixed part falls from 2.25 percent to 0.22 percent, but the proportional part stays at 2.48 percent. Total toll about 2.70 percent, plus the 0.42 percent observed drift, is still about -3.1 percent. SIZE DOES NOT CHANGE THE SIGN.
WITHDRAWN_consequence_do_not_quote.what_that_means_for_b19c_and_b19g: the capacity studies, already declared not runnable at the raised ceiling, would not have changed the conclusion had they run. That is stated here so their loss is not overestimated -- and it was NOT known when they were declared unrunnable, so it is a consolation rather than a justification.
WITHDRAWN_consequence_do_not_quote.what_would_have_to_be_true: a signal would have to identify, at t0, the curves that move more than 2.5 percent in its favour within the holding window. B19F's p90 at immediate exit is about +2.0 percent, so roughly a tenth of launches do move materially -- the question is entirely whether anything observable at t0 predicts WHICH, and the five features tested do not.

WITHDRAWN_decomposition_do_not_quote.WITHDRAWN: superseded by corrected_decomposition. Omits curve slippage entirely and computes the exit fee on the wrong base; its 0.42% residual also has the WRONG SIGN. Kept so the error is visible, NOT to be quoted.

ata_rent_entry_only.note: b10a charges it and deliberately never credits it back, because the reclaim is real but conditional on closing the account. Crediting it would understate cost; not crediting it overstates cost for an operator who does close accounts.

WITHDRAWN_decomposition_do_not_quote.reading: the median immediate-exit outcome is approximately 92 percent TOLL and 8 percent market. The launches are not moving against the position; the position is paying a fee to enter and a fee to leave.

author: codex seat

corrected_decomposition.method: priced through b10a.price_entry and b10a.price_exit against an unchanged curve state, so every component is the kernel's own arithmetic rather than a hand model of it
corrected_decomposition.reading: the median outcome is approximately 105 percent toll, offset by a small favourable drift. The launches are not moving against the position at the median; the toll simply exceeds what the market gives back.

error_1_slippage_omitted_entirely.how_it_was_found: by pricing a round trip through b10a's own kernel instead of arithmetic on constants.
error_1_slippage_omitted_entirely.right: a round trip against an UNCHANGED curve still loses to CURVE SLIPPAGE: buying moves up the bonding curve and selling moves back down it, so gross proceeds on a 0.1 SOL position are 99,337,747 rather than 100,000,000. That is 0.66% of the position and it was missing from the model.
error_1_slippage_omitted_entirely.wrong: the decomposition counted protocol fees, ATA rent and network fees, and attributed everything else to price movement.

error_2_exit_fee_base.right: entry fees are charged ON TOP of the curve input (b10a: lamports_out_of_wallet = quote_in + fees + execution), and the exit fee is charged on actual gross proceeds.
error_2_exit_fee_base.wrong: exit fee computed on (position - entry fee), i.e. as though the entry fee came out of the curve input.

error_3_the_residual_had_the_WRONG_SIGN.right: the true toll is 5.403% against an observed median loss of 5.156%, so the residual is +0.248% and the market moved slightly IN FAVOUR of the position at the median.
error_3_the_residual_had_the_WRONG_SIGN.why_it_matters: the original wording said the launches drift against you. They do not. The loss is MORE than fully explained by the toll, and the market is roughly neutral -- which strengthens rather than weakens the conclusion, and would have been quoted as evidence of adverse selection that does not exist.
error_3_the_residual_had_the_WRONG_SIGN.wrong: residual of 0.42% reported as price movement AGAINST the position.

corrections_applied_2026_08_10.why_this_block_exists: the first version of this finding was computed by hand from the cost constants and was wrong in three ways. It is corrected in place with the errors named, because a finding whose arithmetic was quietly repaired is worth less than one that shows what it got wrong.

not_claimed.a_recommendation_to_trade: none is made, at any size.
not_claimed.that_no_strategy_can_work: this says the five signals tested, priced through this cost model, do not clear the fee floor on this window. It is not a proof that no observable does.
not_claimed.that_the_fee_floor_is_permanent: 125 bps per leg is what this window's curves charged. A different venue, a different program version or a different fee regime would have a different floor, and the arithmetic would have to be redone rather than assumed.

provenance.b19f_cell_cited: E_FIRST_OBSERVATION|delay_1|base -- the least-selected rule in the family, admitting 1,815 of 3,932 curves
provenance.no_pass_spent: this uses the cost constants frozen in B15D_SHADOW_ROUTE_V1, the fee schedules already reported in the B19D/B19F window provenance, and the single median already published in B19F's sealed artifact. Nothing new was read from the evaluation window.

status: FINAL as corrected. V1's arithmetic was wrong in three ways, all named in corrections_applied_2026_08_10 and all kept visible rather than repaired silently.

the_charged_fee_is_125_bps_per_leg_and_i.coverage: 1,435 + 1,761 = 3,196, which is EVERY priceable curve in the window. 125 bps per leg is universal here, not modal, so the floor below is not an average over a spread.
the_charged_fee_is_125_bps_per_leg_and_i.what_is_charged: b10a.curve_fees charges fee + creator_fee + cashback. buyback_fee is REPORTED, NOT CHARGED -- it is a split of the protocol fee, and adding it would double-charge the user by half of it. This was got wrong once while producing this finding and corrected against b10a's source before anything was concluded.

the_hurdle_expressed_as_a_number_CORRECT: at the frozen 0.1 SOL position a strategy must find more than 5.4 percent of favourable round-trip movement to break even, not the 2.5 percent the first version stated -- that figure counted only the protocol fee and omitted slippage and fixed costs. The best case across sizes is about 5.0 percent near 0.25 SOL. For scale, B19F's p90 at immediate exit is about +2.0 percent, which is well below the hurdle at every size tried.

the_size_question_answered_without_the_c.caveat: one synthetic state with 50 SOL of real quote reserve. The direction is driven by constant-product mechanics rather than by this state, but the exact optimum is not a measured property of the cohort and must not be quoted as one.
the_size_question_answered_without_the_c.method: the same kernel round trip, repeated at increasing position sizes against one representative curve state
the_size_question_answered_without_the_c.relationship_to_b19c_and_b19g: this is the shape those studies were built to measure, obtained here for one representative state without spending a pass. It is NOT a substitute for them: a single state is not the cohort's distribution, and the capacity question -- what the OBSERVED book could absorb, cell by cell -- remains unmeasured.
the_size_question_answered_without_the_c.supersedes_the_earlier_claim: the first version said size does not change the sign because the proportional protocol fee is constant. That was right by accident. The real reason is stronger: beyond about 0.25 SOL, TRADING LARGER IS ACTIVELY WORSE, because slippage on a bonding curve grows faster than fixed costs amortise.
the_size_question_answered_without_the_c.the_shape: the toll FALLS then RISES. Fixed costs amortise up to roughly 0.25 SOL, after which curve slippage grows superlinearly and overwhelms the saving. At 1 SOL the toll is worse than at 0.1 SOL; at 5 SOL it is catastrophic.

why_this_is_recorded_separately: B19D and B19F each answer their own question and neither answers this one. Both report that the outcome is negative; neither decomposes WHERE the loss comes from. That decomposition turns out to decide what is worth doing next, so it is written down rather than left in a conversation.
